consensus_expectations: Sell-side is bullish: mean target price $409.81, median $440, range $125.00-$600.00, 39-40 analysts, 'Outperform' recommendation (2.35/5: 17 Buy, 6 Outperform, 17 Hold, 2 Underperform, 4 Sell, 4 No Opinion), implying +28.2% upside from $319.69 [_pool_extracts/Tesla-IncNasdaqGSTSLAEstimatesReport__Consensus.txt]. Consensus EPS Normalized goes $1.83 (FY2026) -> $3.08 (FY2027, +69%) -> $5.83 (FY2028, +89%) -- the Street's own numbers already assume the autonomy/robotics story starts paying off within 24 months, with no disclosed segment economics to underwrite that assumption [same source; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md]. FY2026 revenue estimates have been revised up every lookback window (+20 net analyst revisions in the last month, $102.6bn->$105.4bn) on four consecutive quarterly revenue beats, but every profit line (EBITDA, EBIT, EPS Normalized, EPS GAAP) has net-negative revision breadth even one month after the Q2 2026 miss -- the profitability bar has been cut hard (FY2026 EPS Normalized down 10.7% in a month) but analysts are still cutting, not done cutting [earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §4-5,7]. Tesla issues no formal point guidance for revenue/EBITDA/EPS; management's only quantified figure is a capex floor ('more than $25 billion' for FY2026), which consensus ($26.17bn) already exceeds [earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §2-3].
market_implied_expectations: The reverse-DCF (valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md), holding WACC (12.38%), terminal growth (1.0%), FCF base ($5,762mm TTM) and the 7-year horizon fixed at 04_intrinsic-dcf.md's own values, solves for the growth the $319.69 price / $1,235,847.8mm enterprise value requires: a 68.9% compound annual free-cash-flow growth rate sustained for 7 years (executed via scipy.optimize.brentq). Equivalently, this is about 9.3 years at Tesla's own best-ever annual growth rate (51.4%, FY2022) before fading to terminal growth -- roughly 4-5x longer than the ~2 years Tesla has ever actually sustained a rate near that. A pure-margin channel cannot get there at all: even a 100%-of-revenue EBIT margin on Tesla's own guided revenue/capex path reaches only $1,026,364mm of PV, short of the $1,235,848mm target (implied margin would need to be 119.5% of revenue -- not economically possible). A market-ceiling sanity check converts the 68.9% FCF-CAGR solve to a revenue path and finds it implies Tesla capturing 75-100%+ of the entire global automotive industry (~$2.75tn 2025 market) by FY2032 -- a share no automaker has ever held (Tesla's own 2025 global BEV share was 8.8%, already below BYD's 12.1%). Robustness checks show the FCF-base assumption (19.3pp swing) dominates the WACC (6.2pp) and terminal-g (1.9pp) swings; even at the most favorable FCF-base and WACC combination inside a defensible range, the implied CAGR stays in the 55-65% band -- still 3-4x Tesla's own 5-year historical revenue CAGR (15.2%).
engine_view: The valuation module's triangulated base-case fair value is $32.37/share (bull $336.08 / bear-headline structural-reset $6.86, with a secondary cyclical-trough bear of $20.90), built from three independently-constructed, economically-grounded methods that converge in the same direction: peer relative valuation ($40.19, 1.3x quality-adjusted NTM EV/Sales vs named peers Ford/GM/BYD), segment sum-of-the-parts ($41.09, blended 1.38x forward EV/Sales), and intrinsic DCF ($8.02, terminal-dominated at 125.2% of EV, capped-weight cross-check) [valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md; 99_valuation-synthesis.md]. Tesla's own 5-year trading-multiple history ($286.5 reversion) is deliberately excluded from the weighted base (0% weight) as circular -- it reverts price to what TSLA has always traded for, the exact thing being tested -- and is repurposed as the bull-case input instead. This produces a base-case margin of safety of -887.7% (no cushion, a large embedded premium) and 97.9% downside to the bear case. The engine's decision is Short Candidate, expressed only as a small, defined-risk position (long-dated puts/put spreads, not naked short stock) given an undated catalyst and real squeeze risk -- probability-weighted expected return +56.6% (short-signed), risk/reward 1.85 using the stock's own 5-year multiple ceiling ($417.40) as the adverse case rather than the naive fundamentals-only bull case [final_thesis.md §2, §14; decision_record.json].
what_everyone_knows: Tesla trades at an enormous premium to every named auto peer (roughly 800-2,300% across P/E, EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, and EV/Sales), and bulls have argued for a decade this is an AI/robotics platform, not a car company, while bears have argued the opposite for just as long. Sell-side consensus is itself bullish (mean target $409.81, +28.2% implied upside, Outperform rating). None of this is new information [final_thesis.md §4; valuation/03_relative-valuation-peers.md §3].
what_is_priced_in: Consensus itself already prices an acceleration -- EPS Normalized from $1.83 (FY2026) to $3.08 (FY2027, +69%) to $5.83 (FY2028, +89%) -- i.e. the Street's own numbers assume the autonomy/robotics story starts paying off within 24 months despite zero disclosed segment economics for robotaxi/FSD/Optimus. The reverse-DCF shows the price itself (independent of consensus EPS estimates) requires a 68.9% 7-year FCF CAGR, or capture of most of the global automotive industry by FY2032 [final_thesis.md §4; valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md].
what_market_may_be_missing: (1) The precise, checkable magnitude of what the price requires (68.9% 7-year FCF CAGR / ~9.3 years at Tesla's own best-ever growth rate / a market-ceiling requiring 75-100%+ of the global auto industry) -- a specific quantification, not just a qualitative 'it's expensive' view. (2) The moat is not merely unproven but confirmed eroding: return on capital has fallen every year for three straight years (18.6% -> 8.9% -> 6.0% -> 2.9% -> 2.75%), even on the more forgiving 5-year through-cycle average [business-model/09_moat.md]. (3) A specific overlap most narrative-level bear commentary does not draw: the unresolved federal securities-fraud class action names the CEO personally over alleged misrepresentation of the exact Autopilot/FSD/Robotaxi claims the optionality premium depends on (RF-MGT-005), compounded by a board-enacted entrenchment sequence (Texas reincorporation, a new 3%-of-shares derivative-suit threshold, a supermajority bylaw blocking a majority-backed declassification vote, RF-SHR-002) that narrows the legal tool that could hold the CEO accountable on those exact claims [final_thesis.md §4; management-governance/99].
evidence_engine_is_different: Three independently-built, economically-grounded valuation methods (peer comps, segment SOTP, DCF) converge in the same direction, with peers and SOTP landing within 2% of each other ($40.19 vs $41.09) despite different construction methods -- corroborating, not circular, evidence. The reverse-DCF is an executed, reproducible solve (scipy.optimize.brentq, shown with code and output) tying the implied growth rate to a market-ceiling sanity check against named external data (global auto TAM, Tesla's own 8.8% BEV share vs BYD's 12.1%). The moat deterioration is a filed-data trend (ROIC series over 5 years, 210-885bps below WACC on every basis computed), not an opinion. The litigation/governance overlap (RF-MGT-005, RF-SHR-002) is drawn from primary disclosure (management-governance module, sourced to the litigation and bylaw record), not web commentary. Set against this: the engine's own final_thesis explicitly scores its variant-perception 'edge' at only 40/100 and states it 'largely quantifies and sharpens a bear case sophisticated investors already hold... does not clear the genuinely non-consensus, proven bar the doctrine reserves for edge scores >=50' [final_thesis.md §4]. The distinguishing evidence here is a precise, checkable magnitude and a specific governance/litigation overlap layered on a well-known bear thesis -- not a fact invisible to the market.
base_rate_check: The reverse-DCF explicitly tests the implied growth against Tesla's own history and industry base rates rather than treating it as achievable by assumption: Tesla's FY2021-2025 revenue CAGR was 15.2% (FY2025 itself was -2.9%, an outright decline); its best-ever 2-year burst was 51-71% off a depressed pandemic base, immediately followed by deceleration every year since. The 68.9% CAGR the price requires sits 3-4x above the CAGR implied even at the most favorable FCF-base/WACC combination, and the market-ceiling check shows no automaker in history has ever captured the majority-to-entirety of the global auto industry that the implied revenue trajectory would require. The bear-cyclical scenario is itself base-rate-anchored to the 2008-09 auto-industry downturn (20-30% demand decline, GM/Chrysler required government support) as a named analog because Tesla has under one full standalone cycle of its own data [valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md §3-4; valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md]. This respects CLAUDE.md §9: the burden was placed on the evidence for an exceptional (68.9% CAGR) forecast, and the evidence does not clear that bar -- the price, not the engine, is the one making the exceptional claim without exceptional support.
